assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new door: a tunable platform where flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity can be switched by a twist angle and a gate. It was seen in transport and imaged by scanning probes, and it spawned a whole field of moire quantum materials. The decisive original experiment is the 2018 correlated-insulator and superconductivity observation.
assessment.attribution: Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original experimental discovery. MacDonald (with Bistritzer) predicted the magic angle and flat bands in 2011, which guided the experiment. Andrei's STM work showed twist-induced flat bands and Van Hove singularities earlier and independently, and her role is a real part of the historical record. Bistritzer is a close co-author of MacDonald's prediction and would be left out of a three-person prize. Jarillo-Herrero, MacDonald and Andrei is the most defensible set, but the allocation of credit needs careful checking of who did what first.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the correlated phases and superconductivity in twisted bilayers over several years. The interpretation of the superconducting pairing is still debated, but the discovery itself is solid. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the early STM flat-band observations by Andrei carry the same weight as the 2018 transport discovery.
Bistritzer's exclusion from a three-person prize.
The mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved, though the observation is not in doubt.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines the magic-wavelength lattice with many atoms interrogated at once. It brought fractional frequency uncertainty to the 1e-18 level and enabled tests of relativity, searches for varying constants, and relativistic geodesy. It is a clear invention with strong benefit to measurement science and a likely route to a redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept in 2001-2003 and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock. Ye's group built the systems that reached the best accuracy and showed their physical reach. The credited set has only two names, which is a clean fit and avoids padding. Hall and Haensch already received the 2005 prize for the frequency comb, so the field has history.
assessment.maturity: Several independent labs (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) have confirmed the performance, and comparisons between clocks are routine. Recognition is timely, since the technology is mature and not yet formally adopted for the definition of the second.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as an incremental improvement on earlier atomic clocks and the frequency comb, which was already recognised.
Possible credit to other people, such as theorists of the magic-wavelength idea or Ye's collaborators, is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic force microscopy with qPlus sensors and CO-functionalised tips gives sub-molecular, bond-resolved images of single molecules and on-surface reactions. It is a new tool that opens a door to seeing chemical structure directly, in the spirit of earlier microscopy prizes. The impact on surface science, molecular electronics and on-surface synthesis is large, and I can judge the instrumentation firsthand.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented and developed the qPlus sensor, which made stable small-amplitude, high-resolution force microscopy possible. Gross and Meyer at IBM Zurich showed the 2009 bond-resolved imaging with CO tips. This is a clean three-person split between the sensor invention and the functionalised-tip experiment. Other contributors, for example early STM and AFM inventors who were already recognised in 1986, do not hold a claim here.
assessment.maturity: The method is reproduced in many labs worldwide, and results are routinely cross-checked against theory and other probes. The field is about fifteen years old and stable.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers this a physics discovery or a chemistry-oriented technique.
Interpretation of image contrast in terms of bond order has been debated, though imaging itself is not in doubt.
Whether the prize would be seen as too incremental after the 1986 STM and AFM prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect introduced a new class of matter with protected edge or surface states and changed how we classify electronic phases. The theoretical proposal was followed by experiments that confirmed helical edge channels and surface Dirac states. The impact is broad across condensed matter and materials physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original 2005 theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect. Molenkamp's group made the first experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells in 2007, following the prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who are not in the supplied credit. Hasan carried out the first ARPES observation of 3D topological insulator surface states, which is a strong independent experiment, but a three-person prize cannot hold everyone. I would take Kane, Mele and Molenkamp as the core and flag Hasan, and the missing theorists, as unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have confirmed the HgTe edge transport and the Bi-based surface states, and the interpretation is well established. Recognition is mature, perhaps overdue relative to the 2016 prize for topological phase transitions.
uncertainties: Credit split among Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (not in the list), Molenkamp and Hasan is truly contested.
Fu and Kane, and the 3D theory, are not covered by the supplied names.
Overlap with ballot entries B038 and B042 on quantum anomalous Hall.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices are programmable quantum many-body systems that realise Hubbard models. The experimental breakthrough was the observation of the superfluid-to-Mott insulator transition and later fermionic and microscope experiments with single-site resolution. It gives a new tool for studying phenomena inaccessible in solids.
assessment.attribution: The first superfluid-Mott experiment was by Greiner and Bloch with Haensch's group in 2002, following the Jaksch-Zoller proposal. Esslinger's group led the fermionic Mott and band-insulator work. Cirac and Zoller proposed the quantum simulation concept, which is theoretically seminal, but if the prize rewards the original experiment, the experimentalists should come first. Zoller's contribution is also credited on other entries, so the allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories with continued progress, and quantum gas microscopes have given independent verification. Recognition is somewhat overdue relative to the 2001 BEC prize and the 2012 prize for quantum control of single particles.
uncertainties: Zoller and Cirac's theoretical role versus the experimentalists is not settled in a three-person limit.
Haensch's group and Jaksch are not in the supplied names.
Concern that quantum simulation is a broad programme rather than one discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Anyons, particles with fractional statistics in two dimensions, are a fundamental extension of the boson-fermion dichotomy. Fractional charge was measured in shot noise and later anyonic statistics were seen in interferometry and collider experiments. The result matters for understanding fractional quantum Hall states and topological quantum computation.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim made the 1977 prediction of fractional statistics in low dimensions, an original theoretical idea. Heiblum's group made the first shot-noise measurement of fractional charge in 1997 and developed the interferometers. Fève and Manfra contributed to the later statistics demonstrations, so the credit is spread over many hands. The Laughlin-type quantum Hall prize of 1998 already covers fractional charge in the underlying phase, which complicates the novelty argument.
assessment.maturity: Anyonic braiding statistics were convincingly demonstrated only around 2020, and results continue to be refined. Fractional charge is mature, but statistics are young. Some may judge the recognition premature.
uncertainties: Whether the experimental statistics evidence is strong enough yet, because the 2020 results come from few groups.
Overlap with the 1998 prize for the fractional quantum Hall effect.
Attribution between theory pioneers (also Wilczek and Halperin) and experimentalists is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions, and the later giant effect in crystalline MgO, underpins hard-disk read heads and magnetic random access memory. It is a device-level discovery with large benefit to technology and a clear experimental basis.
assessment.attribution: Moodera and Miyazaki independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995, which is the original experiment. Yuasa (and Parkin) demonstrated the large MgO effect in 2004. Parkin's name is also credited here but I would leave him out of a three-person set, at some risk. The credit between amorphous-barrier and MgO discoveries could justify different recognition for the two parts.
assessment.maturity: The effect is thoroughly confirmed and industrially deployed for around two decades. The 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance partly overlaps in subject, so some may see the topic as already honoured.
uncertainties: The relation to the 2007 GMR prize and whether this is seen as a follow-on.
The compound nature, with the original TMR and MgO as separate discoveries needing different credit.
Parkin's exclusion and Julliere's earlier low-temperature result are not covered by the names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and control of single defect spins, notably nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond, opened a way to measure magnetic fields, temperature and strain with nanometre resolution, including in biological samples. It is a new tool in the sense I value, bringing quantum sensing into microscopy.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group first detected a single NV centre spin optically in 1997, which is the original experiment. Awschalom and Lukin built the coherent control and sensing programmes, but their contributions are later and broader. Walsworth is also credited. The three-name set is plausible but contestable, since the sensing ideas were developed by several groups in parallel.
assessment.maturity: Results are reproduced in many laboratories and applications are growing, though the technology is still under development. Recognition would be somewhat early for the sensing applications.
uncertainties: Whether the original detection or the later sensing programme is the discovery to honour.
Credit among Wrachtrup, Awschalom, Lukin, Walsworth and Gruber/Jelezko (not in list) is uncertain.
Lukin is credited on other topics as well.
